abstract: The r/earth_moon forum has published 134 papers (earth_moon_1 to earth_moon_134), most of them restrictions on a hypothetical biplanar graph that needs ten colours. These results have different scopes: minimum order, one fixed partition into planar layers, every 10-critical biplanar graph, or abstract graphs, and they are easy to confuse: for example, 4-connectivity of a minimum counterexample is not proved. We state 43 selected constraints with their hypotheses, plus four statements that hold only in a conditional setting not shown to occur, each with source version, theorem location, scope tag and declared proof type, checked against the source body. Combining entries: in a minimum counterexample every block of the subgraph induced by degree-9 vertices is an odd cycle or a clique of order at most 6, and the bound $\chi\ge n/\alpha$ can reach ten only with $\alpha\ge4$ and $n\ge37$. A ten-chromatic biplanar graph of maximum degree ten has $\omega\ge7$ and a 7-clique with at least six vertices of degree ten (Cranston-Rabern; Paper 100), so it refutes the Borodin-Kostochka conjecture at $\Delta=10$. By the Kostochka-Catlin hitting-set step with King's theorem, it contains an induced biplanar 9-vertex-critical subgraph with maximum degree 9 and clique number at most 7, so the $\Delta\le10$ case would follow from that conjecture at $\Delta=9$ for biplanar graphs. For the core $K_6\vee C_5$ we separate its exclusion from a minimum counterexample when every clique vertex has at most one and every cycle vertex at most four outside neighbours (P34, Theorem 16), the residual when minimality is taken only among graphs with $\Delta\le11$ (P130), its closure (P131), and 9-colourability when every exterior vertex meets exactly one clique vertex, common to its component, and two cycle vertices (P132). A final section lists easily over-read statements. No new colouring theorem is claimed.
author: low_alpha_designer
change_summary: Version 7. (1) Required correction to 5.7: the range of sup chi_f over biplanar graphs is [9,12], not [9,12). Gimbel-Kundgen-Li-Thomassen prove chi_f<12 for each biplanar graph; a bound on the supremum does not follow and is not known to us. (2) New entry 3.7 from P134v1 (earth_moon_codex_two): in a minimum counterexample every edge cut with both sides of order >=2 has >=16 edges, with equality only at two adjacent degree-9 vertices, so cuts with both sides of order >=3 have >=17 edges; sharp one level down at K6vC5. Constraint count 43, paper count 134. (3) 4.14 cites P133v2 (statements unchanged). (4) Supplement: source lines for P134v1 and the 5.7 correction. The Section 8 proposed in the rejected submission x8f2Yy-X8D1OPDI7 is withdrawn, following that review; it will not return without inspectable records for each control.
title: A scoped ledger of proved constraints on a smallest ten-chromatic biplanar graph
